Arugula.tip: Bolts quickly in heat; succession sow every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest.
Arugula.harvest_cues: Leaves 2-3 inches; harvest before flowering for mildest flavor.
Arugula.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; keep dry.

Asparagus.tip: Plant 1- or 2-year crowns; don't harvest first 2 years to build root strength.
Asparagus.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; balanced spring + phosphorus after harvest season.
Asparagus.harvest_cues: Spears 6-8 inches, pencil-thick; snap at base. Harvest 2-4 weeks (young bed).
Asparagus.storage: Fridge upright in water up to 5 days.

Avocados.tip: Zones 9-11 only — protect from frost when young.

Basil.tip: Pinch flowers to keep leaves coming.
Basil.fertilizer: Light balanced; avoid high nitrogen (reduces flavor).
Basil.harvest_cues: Pinch above leaf node; harvest before flowering.
Basil.storage: Store in water on counter 1 week; freeze in oil for long term.

Beans.tip: Do not start indoors — direct sow only.
Beans.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); light phosphorus at planting.
Beans.harvest_cues: Pods firm and filled out; snap cleanly.
Beans.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; blanch and freeze for longer.

Beets.tip: Each 'seed' is a cluster — thin to 3-4 in after sprouting.
Beets.harvest_cues: Roots 1.5-3 inches diameter; greens edible at any size.
Beets.storage: Fridge up to 3 weeks; remove tops.

Bok Choy.tip: Quick cool-season crop; bolt-resistant varieties extend harvest.
Bok Choy.harvest_cues: Leaves full and crisp; cut at base before bolting.
Bok Choy.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; keeps best unwashed.

Broccoli.tip: Harvest before florets start to open.
Broccoli.harvest_cues: Head tight and dark green; cut before florets open.
Broccoli.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; blanch and freeze.

Brussels Sprouts.tip: Start early for fall harvest; flavor improves after frost.
Brussels Sprouts.fertilizer: High nitrogen; side-dress monthly, reduce once heads form.
Brussels Sprouts.harvest_cues: Sprouts firm and 1-2 inches; harvest from bottom up as they mature.
Brussels Sprouts.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; blanch and freeze.

Cabbage.tip: Even moisture prevents heads from splitting.
Cabbage.harvest_cues: Head firm and dense; squeeze — it should feel solid.
Cabbage.storage: Fridge up to 2 months; don't wash until use.

Carrots.tip: Loose, deep soil is essential — thin to avoid forking.
Carrots.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; moderate phosphorus and potassium.
Carrots.harvest_cues: Shoulders visible at soil surface; orange and firm.
Carrots.storage: Fridge up to 3 weeks; remove tops first.

Cauliflower.tip: Tie outer leaves over the head to blanch it white.
Cauliflower.harvest_cues: Head 6-8 inches, compact and white; cut before curds separate.
Cauliflower.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; blanch and freeze.

Celeriac.tip: Start indoors 10-12 weeks early; needs long cool season and consistent moisture.
Celeriac.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; high nitrogen throughout season.
Celeriac.harvest_cues: Root 3-4 inches across; firm and aromatic. Flavor peaks after light frost.
Celeriac.storage: Fridge up to 1 month; stores well in cool cellar.

Celery.tip: Needs consistently moist soil — mulch heavily.
Celery.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; high nitrogen throughout season.
Celery.harvest_cues: Stalks 8+ inches; cut outer stalks first or harvest whole.
Celery.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; wrap in foil to prevent drying.

Chard.tip: Cut outer leaves and the plant keeps producing.
Chard.harvest_cues: Outer leaves 6-8 inches; cut at base.
Chard.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; stems and leaves store separately.

Chives.tip: Perennial in zones 3+; divide clumps every 3 years to reinvigorate.
Chives.harvest_cues: Snip leaves 2-3 inches from base; harvest before flowering.
Chives.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; freeze chopped for long term.

Cilantro.tip: Bolts quickly — succession sow every 3 weeks. The dried seed is coriander.
Cilantro.harvest_cues: Leaves ferny and 6+ inches; harvest before flowering.
Cilantro.storage: Fridge in water up to 1 week; freeze packed in oil.

Collard Greens.tip: More heat-tolerant than kale; harvest outer leaves for continuous production.
Collard Greens.harvest_cues: Outer leaves 8-10 inches; pick lower leaves first.
Collard Greens.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; blanch and freeze.

Corn.tip: Plant in blocks of 4+ rows for good pollination.
Corn.fertilizer: Heavy nitrogen feeder; side-dress at knee height.
Corn.harvest_cues: Silks brown and dry; kernels plump and milky when punctured.
Corn.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; eat as soon as possible for best flavor.

Cucumbers.tip: Trellis vining types to save space.
Cucumbers.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; side-dress with nitrogen when vining.
Cucumbers.harvest_cues: Dark green and firm; pick before yellowing.
Cucumbers.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; do not freeze.

Dill.tip: Direct sow — dislikes transplanting. Succession sow for continuous harvest.
Dill.harvest_cues: Harvest leaves before flowering; seeds when heads turn brown.
Dill.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; dry or freeze for long term.

Edamame.tip: Harvest at the green stage before pods dry — pick when plump and bright.
Edamame.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); balanced at planting.
Edamame.harvest_cues: Pods plump and bright green, 3 inches long; beans visible through pod.
Edamame.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; blanch and freeze for longer.

Eggplant.tip: Needs warm soil — wait until nights stay above 55°F.
Eggplant.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; side-dress with nitrogen mid-season.
Eggplant.harvest_cues: Skin glossy and slightly springy; don't let it go dull.
Eggplant.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; best used fresh.

Endive.tip: Cover heads for 2 weeks before harvest to blanch and mellow the flavor.
Endive.harvest_cues: Head firm and full; blanch if desired before cutting.
Endive.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; one of the longest-storing salad greens.

Fava Beans.tip: Cool-season legume — direct sow 4-6 weeks before last frost; tolerates light frost.
Fava Beans.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); light phosphorus at planting.
Fava Beans.harvest_cues: Pods fat and filled; beans inside clear with no dark ring.
Fava Beans.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; shell and freeze for longer.

Fennel.tip: Grow in isolation — allelopathic to most vegetables. Keep away from all food crops.
Fennel.fertilizer: Light balanced; too much fertility reduces flavor.
Fennel.harvest_cues: Bulb 3-5 inches across; fronds harvestable anytime before bolting.
Fennel.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; fronds dry well.

Garlic.tip: Plant cloves in fall, pointy end up.
Garlic.fertilizer: Nitrogen in spring; stop fertilizing by early summer.
Garlic.harvest_cues: Bottom 3-4 leaves brown; dig before all leaves die back.
Garlic.storage: Cure 3-4 weeks in warm, dry place; store up to 6 months.

Ginger.tip: Zones 8b+ outdoor; elsewhere start in pots and bring indoors before frost.
Ginger.harvest_cues: Leaves yellow and die back in fall; dig after first frost threat.
Ginger.storage: Fridge up to 1 month; freeze grated; dry and grind.

Globe Artichoke.tip: Perennial zones 7+; in cold zones start early indoors and treat as annual.
Globe Artichoke.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; balanced monthly during growing season.
Globe Artichoke.harvest_cues: Buds before they open; tight scales and firm; cut 1-2 inches below head.

Green Onions.tip: Snip from above — plants regrow; succession sow for continuous harvest.
Green Onions.harvest_cues: Stems pencil-thick; harvest at any size.
Green Onions.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; stand in water to keep fresh.

Ground Cherries.tip: Fruit falls to ground when ripe — fallen fruit inside husk is ready.
Ground Cherries.harvest_cues: Fruit falls to ground; papery husk tan. Check frequently.
Ground Cherries.storage: In husk at room temp 2-3 weeks; fridge in husk 1-2 months.

Horseradish.tip: Plant root pieces in spring; very vigorous — give it dedicated space.
Horseradish.fertilizer: Minimal; top-dress with compost each spring.
Horseradish.harvest_cues: Harvest roots after first frost for best flavor; dig in fall.
Horseradish.storage: Fridge up to 3 months; grate fresh for maximum pungency.

Jerusalem Artichoke.tip: Invasive — plant in a contained bed or large pot to control spread.
Jerusalem Artichoke.harvest_cues: Stalks die back in fall; dig tubers through winter.
Jerusalem Artichoke.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; leave in ground as living pantry.

Kale.tip: Flavor improves after a light frost.
Kale.harvest_cues: Outer leaves 8-10 inches; pick lower leaves first.
Kale.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; remove stems before storing.

Kohlrabi.tip: Harvest when bulb is tennis ball size — larger gets woody.
Kohlrabi.harvest_cues: Bulb 2-3 inches diameter; firm and bright.
Kohlrabi.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; store bulb and leaves separately.

Leeks.tip: Blanch by hilling soil up around stems as they grow.
Leeks.harvest_cues: Shaft 1 inch diameter; blanched white portion 4+ inches.
Leeks.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; or leave in ground until needed.

Lemongrass.tip: Zones 8b+ perennial; root a grocery store stalk in water to start for free.
Lemongrass.harvest_cues: Stalks 1 foot or taller; cut at base; inner stalk white-pale yellow.
Lemongrass.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; dry or freeze stalks.

Lettuce.tip: Bolts in heat — succession sow every 2 weeks.
Lettuce.harvest_cues: Outer leaves firm and full; cut before bolting.
Lettuce.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; keep moist.

Mangoes.fertilizer: Balanced fertilizer 3-4x per year; reduce nitrogen once mature.

Melons.tip: Needs long warm season — start indoors in cool climates.
Melons.fertilizer: Balanced early; switch to low-nitrogen when fruit sets.
Melons.harvest_cues: Sweet smell at stem end; slips off vine with light pressure.
Melons.storage: Counter until ripe; fridge once cut.

Mint.tip: Contain in pots — spreads aggressively by underground runners.
Mint.fertilizer: Light; vigorous grower needs minimal feeding.
Mint.harvest_cues: Leaves 3-4 inches; harvest before flowering for best flavor.
Mint.storage: Fridge in water up to 1 week; dry or freeze.

Mustard Greens.tip: Very fast cool-season crop; sow in fall for mildest flavor.
Mustard Greens.fertilizer: Light nitrogen; quick crop needs minimal feeding.
Mustard Greens.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; best used fresh.

Mâche.tip: Cold-hardy to 5°F — an excellent winter green in cold frames.
Mâche.harvest_cues: Rosettes 3-4 inches across; harvest whole or leaf by leaf.
Mâche.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; very delicate.

Okra.tip: Soak seeds overnight to speed germination.
Okra.harvest_cues: Pods 2-4 inches; pick every 2 days to prevent toughening.
Okra.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; slice and freeze long term.

Onions.tip: Stop watering when tops fall over to cure bulbs.
Onions.fertilizer: High nitrogen early; reduce once bulbing starts.
Onions.harvest_cues: Tops fall over naturally; cure in sun 1-2 weeks.
Onions.storage: Cool, dry, dark place up to 6 months after curing.

Oregano.tip: Perennial zones 5+; slightly stressed plants have stronger flavor.
Oregano.fertilizer: Very light; lean soil improves flavor.
Oregano.harvest_cues: Harvest stems before flowering; cut back by 1/3 maximum.
Oregano.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; dries excellently.

Parsley.tip: Soak seed overnight to speed germination; biennial — best leaf production in year 1.
Parsley.harvest_cues: Stems with 3 leaf segments; harvest outer stems first.
Parsley.storage: Fridge in water up to 2 weeks; dry or freeze for long term.

Parsnips.tip: Sow fresh seed; flavor peaks after frost. Slow to germinate — be patient.
Parsnips.fertilizer: Moderate balanced; avoid excess nitrogen (causes forking).
Parsnips.harvest_cues: Roots 8-12 inches; sweetest after a hard frost.
Parsnips.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; or leave in ground under mulch.

Peanuts.tip: Zones 6b+ for reliable harvest; hill soil as plants flower — pods develop underground.
Peanuts.fertilizer: Low nitrogen (fixes own); high calcium helps pod fill.
Peanuts.harvest_cues: Leaves yellow; dig and check a pod — inner hull ridged and full.
Peanuts.storage: Dry in shell 2-3 weeks, then cure; store months in cool dry place.

Peas.tip: Direct sow as soon as soil can be worked in spring.
Peas.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; light phosphorus at planting.
Peas.harvest_cues: Pods plump and filled; pick daily to encourage production.
Peas.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; blanch and freeze for longer.

Peppers.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; reduce nitrogen when fruiting.
Peppers.harvest_cues: Green or wait until fully colored; firm and glossy.
Peppers.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; freeze for long term.

Potatoes.tip: Hill soil as vines grow to increase yield; stop watering when tops die back.
Potatoes.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; side-dress when plants are 6 inches tall.
Potatoes.harvest_cues: Skin set (doesn't rub off easily); dig after tops die back.
Potatoes.storage: Cool, dark, dry place 2-3 months; cure 1 week at 55°F first.

Pumpkins.tip: Each plant needs 50+ sq ft — plan space accordingly.
Pumpkins.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; balanced at planting, low-nitrogen once flowering.
Pumpkins.harvest_cues: Deep color and hard rind; stem dry and corky.
Pumpkins.storage: Cool, dry place 2-3 months; do not freeze.

Radishes.tip: Fastest crop in the garden — great row markers.
Radishes.harvest_cues: Roots 1 inch diameter; pull before getting pithy.
Radishes.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; remove tops.

Rhubarb.tip: Don't harvest first year; NEVER eat the leaves — they are toxic.
Rhubarb.fertilizer: Balanced in spring; compost mulch annually.
Rhubarb.harvest_cues: Stalks 12-18 inches; pull and twist — never cut more than 1/3 of plant.
Rhubarb.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; chops and freezes well.

Rosemary.tip: Perennial zones 7+; grow in pots elsewhere and overwinter indoors.
Rosemary.fertilizer: Very light; excess fertilizer reduces flavor and fragrance.
Rosemary.harvest_cues: Snip tips 3-4 inches; harvest before or just after flowering.
Rosemary.storage: Fridge 2 weeks; dry bundles or freeze for long term.

Rutabaga.tip: Direct sow early summer for fall harvest; frost improves sweetness.
Rutabaga.harvest_cues: Roots 3-5 inches; harvest after first frost for best flavor.
Rutabaga.storage: Fridge up to 3 weeks; root cellar several months.

Sage.tip: Perennial zones 4+; prune hard in spring to prevent woodiness.
Sage.fertilizer: Very light; excess fertility reduces flavor.
Sage.harvest_cues: Harvest leaves before or just after flowering.
Sage.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; dries and freezes well.

Shallots.tip: Plant sets in fall (mild climates) or early spring (cold climates).
Shallots.fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen; reduce once bulbing starts.
Shallots.harvest_cues: Tops fall and yellow; cure 2-3 weeks in warm dry spot.
Shallots.storage: Cool, dry, dark place up to 6 months after curing.

Spinach.tip: Cool-season crop — sow in early spring or fall.
Spinach.fertilizer: Moderate nitrogen; side-dress lightly once established.
Spinach.harvest_cues: Outer leaves 3+ inches; harvest before heat causes bolting.
Spinach.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; do not wash until use.

Squash.tip: Direct sow after last frost — transplants poorly.
Squash.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; side-dress monthly with balanced fertilizer.
Squash.harvest_cues: Skin resists thumbnail scratch; rich color.
Squash.storage: Cool, dry place up to 3 months (winter squash); fridge 5 days (summer).

Strawberries.tip: Remove first-year flowers on June-bearing types for stronger plants.
Strawberries.fertilizer: Balanced in spring; high phosphorus supports fruiting.
Strawberries.harvest_cues: Fully red all over; slight give; stem snaps cleanly.
Strawberries.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; do not wash until use. Freeze whole.

Sweet Potatoes.tip: Plant slips, not seeds — cure dug roots for 2 weeks.
Sweet Potatoes.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; high potassium at planting.
Sweet Potatoes.harvest_cues: Leaves yellow and vines die back; skin doesn't rub off.
Sweet Potatoes.storage: Cure 10-14 days at 85°F; store at 55-60°F up to 6 months.

Thyme.tip: Perennial zones 5+; excellent ground cover between larger plants.
Thyme.fertilizer: Very light; well-drained soil matters more than fertility.
Thyme.harvest_cues: Harvest leafy stems anytime; just before flowering is strongest.
Thyme.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; dries excellently.

Tomatillos.tip: Need 2 plants for pollination; papery husk bursts when ripe.
Tomatillos.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; low-nitrogen once flowering.
Tomatillos.harvest_cues: Husk fills out fully and starts to split or brown; fruit firm inside.
Tomatillos.storage: Counter in husk 1-2 weeks; fridge up to 3 weeks.

Tomatoes.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; low-nitrogen once flowering.
Tomatoes.harvest_cues: Fully colored and slightly soft; twist to test.
Tomatoes.storage: Counter at room temp; use within 1 week.

Turmeric.tip: Similar to ginger — long season tropical. Start rhizomes indoors 8 weeks early in cool zones.
Turmeric.fertilizer: Monthly balanced; high potassium before harvest.
Turmeric.harvest_cues: Leaves yellow and drop in fall; rhizomes bright orange when scraped.
Turmeric.storage: Fridge up to 1 month; dry and grind; freeze.

Turnips.tip: Thin early for best root development; greens are edible and nutritious.
Turnips.harvest_cues: Roots 2-3 inches; younger is more tender.
Turnips.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; cool cellar up to a month.

Watercress.tip: Needs consistently moist or flowing water; excellent in containers with wet saucers.
Watercress.fertilizer: Light; grows well in nutrient-rich water.
Watercress.harvest_cues: Stems 6-8 inches; harvest tips to encourage bushiness.
Watercress.storage: Fridge in water up to 5 days.

Zucchini.tip: Pick when 6-8 inches for best flavour; plants produce rapidly in peak season.
Zucchini.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; side-dress with nitrogen mid-season.
Zucchini.harvest_cues: 6-8 inches long; skin tender and easily pierced.
Zucchini.storage: Fridge up to 5 days; best eaten fresh.

Microgreens.tip: Grow in shallow trays; harvest with scissors just above the soil line.
Microgreens.fertilizer: None needed — use quality potting mix.
Microgreens.harvest_cues: First true leaves emerging; typically 1-3 inches tall.
Microgreens.storage: Fridge up to 7 days; keep dry.

Jalapeño.tip: Stress slightly by withholding water near harvest to increase heat.
Jalapeño.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; reduce nitrogen once flowering.
Jalapeño.harvest_cues: Deep green; about 3 inches long. Red when fully ripe and hotter.
Jalapeño.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; freeze or pickle for long term.

Cherry Tomatoes.tip: Indeterminate varieties need staking; pinch suckers for bigger fruit.
Cherry Tomatoes.fertilizer: Balanced at planting; low-nitrogen once flowering.
Cherry Tomatoes.harvest_cues: Fully coloured; squeeze gently — should give slightly.
Cherry Tomatoes.storage: Counter at room temp; use within 5 days.

Sweet Corn.tip: Plant in blocks of 4+ rows for wind pollination; don't grow near field corn.
Sweet Corn.fertilizer: Heavy nitrogen feeder; side-dress at knee height.
Sweet Corn.harvest_cues: Silks brown; kernels plump and milky when pierced.
Sweet Corn.storage: Fridge up to 3 days; eat immediately for best sweetness.

Butternut Squash.tip: Leave on vine until skin is tan and stem has dried; cures off vine for 2 weeks.
Butternut Squash.fertilizer: Heavy feeder; compost at planting and side-dress monthly.
Butternut Squash.harvest_cues: Skin tan and hard; stem dry and corky.
Butternut Squash.storage: Cool, dry place up to 3-6 months.

Raspberries.tip: Summer-fruiting canes: cut spent floricanes to ground after harvest. Autumn canes: cut all to ground in late winter.
Raspberries.fertilizer: Balanced feed in early spring; avoid high nitrogen after midsummer.
Raspberries.harvest_cues: Berries come away easily from the plug; deep colour throughout; sweet aroma.
Raspberries.storage: Fridge 2-3 days; freeze on trays then bag for up to 12 months.

Blueberries.tip: Blueberries demand acidic soil (pH 4.5–5.5). Grow in ericaceous compost or amend heavily with sulphur and bark mulch.
Blueberries.fertilizer: Ericaceous (acidic) fertilizer each spring; no lime ever.
Blueberries.harvest_cues: Fully blue with slight grey bloom; taste test — ripe berries are sweet, not tart.
Blueberries.storage: Fridge up to 2 weeks; freeze for long-term storage.

Blackberries.tip: Thornless varieties (Loch Ness, Chester) are much easier to manage in home gardens. Train canes along wires.
Blackberries.fertilizer: Balanced spring feed; mulch thickly to retain moisture and suppress weeds.
Blackberries.harvest_cues: Fully black and comes away from the plug easily; flesh soft and deeply sweet.
Blackberries.storage: Fridge 3-4 days; freeze immediately if not eating fresh.

Gooseberries.tip: Prune into an open-centred 'goblet' shape each winter to maximise airflow and reduce mildew. Wear thick gloves!
Gooseberries.fertilizer: Balanced NPK in early spring; sulphate of potash in midsummer.
Gooseberries.harvest_cues: For cooking: firm and green. For dessert: fully ripe (yellow, red or white), slightly soft with bloom.
Gooseberries.storage: Fridge 1 week; freeze or jam for long-term.

Redcurrants.tip: Redcurrants fruit on old wood — don't remove old branches indiscriminately. They're more shade-tolerant than other soft fruit.
Redcurrants.fertilizer: Balanced spring feed + high-potash summer feed for best colour and flavour.
Redcurrants.harvest_cues: Whole trusses turn deep red simultaneously; taste test a few berries for balanced sweet-tart flavour.
Redcurrants.storage: Fridge up to 1 week on the truss; freeze whole truss for later.

Nasturtium.tip: Grow in poor soil for maximum flowers — rich soil produces mainly leaves. Both flowers and leaves are peppery and edible.
Nasturtium.fertilizer: Minimal — avoid nitrogen-rich feeds or you get leaves but few flowers.
pests: Aphids (act as trap crop — draw aphids away from vegetables)
Nasturtium.harvest_cues: Flowers open fully; pick in the morning for best flavour. Leaves anytime. Seeds when fat and green for capers.
Nasturtium.storage: Use flowers same day. Seeds pickle as 'poor man's capers' in brine.

Borage.tip: Self-seeds prolifically — deadhead if you don't want it everywhere next year. Blue star flowers are edible; freeze in ice cubes for drinks.
Borage.fertilizer: Unfussy — thrives with minimal feeding. Rich soil reduces flowering.
Borage.harvest_cues: Harvest individual star-shaped flowers when fully open; young leaves are edible before stems become hairy.
Borage.storage: Use flowers immediately; freeze in ice cubes to preserve. Leaves wilt quickly — use same day.

Calendula.tip: Deadhead constantly to extend flowering season well into autumn. The more you pick, the more it blooms.
Calendula.fertilizer: Light; too much nitrogen reduces flowers.
Calendula.harvest_cues: Petals fully open in morning sun; bright orange or yellow. Pick regularly to encourage more blooms.
Calendula.storage: Dry petals on a screen in a cool airy place; store in an airtight jar for months.

Lemon Balm.days: 75-90 days to mature plant (harvest lightly first year)
Lemon Balm.tip: Contain it in a pot if you don't want it spreading — it's very vigorous. Cut back hard after flowering to refresh growth.
Lemon Balm.fertilizer: Minimal — thrives in average soil; over-feeding reduces essential oil potency.
Lemon Balm.harvest_cues: Harvest young leaves before flowering for best lemon scent; cut stems in the morning.
Lemon Balm.storage: Dry leaves in a dark airy place 1-2 weeks; store in airtight jars. Or freeze in ice cubes.

Tarragon.depth: Transplant or division (French variety doesn't set viable seed)
Tarragon.tip: Always grow French (not Russian) tarragon — Russian has little flavour. French tarragon must be grown from cuttings or division, not seed.
Tarragon.fertilizer: Light; excellent in poor, well-drained soil.
Tarragon.harvest_cues: Harvest young shoot tips 3-4 inches long before plant flowers; leaves most flavourful in late spring.
Tarragon.storage: Dry or freeze in ice cubes; makes excellent tarragon vinegar.

Sorrel.tip: Remove flower stalks promptly to keep leaf production going. Leaves are sour — use like spinach to add acidity to soups and sauces.
Sorrel.fertilizer: Light nitrogen once in spring; low-maintenance perennial.
Sorrel.harvest_cues: Pick outer leaves when 4-6 inches long. Leaves are ready all season if flower stalks are removed.
Sorrel.storage: Fridge 3-5 days; blanch and freeze for long-term use in soups.

Chervil.tip: Succession sow every 3 weeks for continuous supply. Bolts quickly in heat — grow in spring, autumn, and under cover in winter.
Chervil.fertilizer: Minimal — light soil with some compost is ideal.
Chervil.harvest_cues: Cut outer leaves before flowering; leaves have a delicate anise flavour and wilt quickly after cutting.
Chervil.storage: Use fresh immediately; fridge 2 days max. Freezes acceptably in ice cubes.
